_about: MT Creative Works forms: the single source of truth for BOTH forms (the quick message and the website brief).

Read by the browser (src/lib/forms.ts imports this file) and by the Vercel function (functions/serverlib/mtcw/form-schema.json is a byte-identical copy made by `npm run sync:form-schema`; never edit the copy by hand).
The exact API, email formats and browser state machine are in docs/build/FORMS-CONTRACT.md. The owner's binding decisions are in docs/build/FORMS-DECISIONS.md.

Keys are stable camelCase and are also the native (no-JavaScript) form field names. Change a label freely; change a key or an option value only together with the browser code, the function and the contract.

labelSource says where each label came from: 'brief' = docs/brief/MTCW-website-brief-form-v01.md word for word, 'owner' = the owner's chat instruction (FORMS-DECISIONS section 1), 'existing-contact-form' = the current /contact/ form (src/content/copy/contact.ts), 'chosen' = plain wording chosen for this schema because the brief gives none.
Message templates: {max} is replaced with the number formatted with toLocaleString('en-GB') (4000 -> '4,000'); {n} is the 1-based position of a repeated item.

origins._rule: Exact string match on the Origin header (scheme + host + optional port). 'Origin: null' and a missing Origin are refused for POST. The localhost patterns apply ONLY when MTCW_MAIL_MODE=sink.

limits.lengthUnit: Unicode code points, counted AFTER sanitising (see text.singleLine / text.multiLine). Over-limit answers are rejected with a message, never truncated.
limits._bodyBytesRationale: Each cap is at least the worst case allowed by the field limits below (every field full of 4-byte characters; x12 for percent-encoding), checked by tests/unit/form-schema.test.ts. fileJson = 3,000,000 bytes as base64 (4,000,000) plus the text fields, and stays under Vercel's 4.5 MB request limit.

rateLimit._scope: Per warm function instance, in memory, keyed by an HMAC of the client IP (never stored or logged raw). NOT sufficient on its own on a distributed host (FORMS-DECISIONS section 6).

dedupe._scope: Per warm instance, in memory. Only successful responses are remembered. A repeat of the same attemptId (contact/brief) or the same ref+index+attemptId (file) returns the remembered response with duplicate:true and sends nothing.

limits._lengthRationale: Names and single-line answers match the existing contact form (name 100, email 254 = RFC 5321 path limit, phone 32, business 120, town 80, website 300). Long answers are sized for a few paragraphs typed on a phone (600-4,000). Sharing links get 500 because cloud-drive links are long. Captions are short (300); the owner's per-photo extra detail gets 2,000.

text.singleLine: Unicode NFC; every line break (CRLF, CR, LF, VT, FF, NEL, U+2028, U+2029) and tab becomes a space; C0/C1 controls and DEL are removed; bidirectional embeddings/overrides/isolates (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069), zero-width space U+200B, word joiner U+2060, BOM U+FEFF and soft hyphen U+00AD are removed (ZWJ/ZWNJ are kept); runs of whitespace collapse to one space; trimmed. Never contains CR or LF. Same as sanitiseSingleLine in src/server/enquiry-schema.ts.
text.multiLine: Unicode NFC; all line breaks become LF; tabs become spaces; the same controls and invisible characters are removed; trailing spaces trimmed per line; 3+ consecutive line breaks collapse to 2; trimmed. Same as sanitiseMultiLine in src/server/enquiry-schema.ts.
text.email: Single-line, then: at most 254 characters; exactly one '@'; local part a dot-atom of [A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-] (max 64); domain of 2+ DNS labels (letters, digits, inner hyphens, each max 63), total max 253, the last label alphabetic (2-63) or punycode (xn--). No quoted local parts, comments, spaces, commas, angle brackets or IP literals. Same as isValidEmail in src/server/enquiry-schema.ts.
text.phone: Single-line, then: only digits, spaces, '+', '(', ')', '.', '-'; '+' only as the first character; 7 to 15 digits in total. Same as isValidPhone in src/server/enquiry-schema.ts.
text.url: Single-line, then normalised WITHOUT fetching: a bare domain gets https:// ('yourbusiness.co.uk' -> 'https://yourbusiness.co.uk/'); '//host' gets https:; only http and https schemes; no spaces, no user:password@, no IP addresses, no single-label hosts; every host label valid and an alphabetic or punycode top-level label; the normalised href must still fit maxLength. Same as normaliseWebsite in src/server/enquiry-schema.ts (whose length limit is LIMITS.website; here it is the field's own maxLength).

honeypot.label: Leave this field empty
honeypot._rule: Off-screen, aria-hidden, tabindex -1, autocomplete off. Top-level key in JSON bodies; a form field in native posts. Any non-blank value: HTTP 400 {ok:false,error:'bad_request'}, nothing is sent, never a success.

attemptId._rule: Made by the browser (crypto.randomUUID without hyphens) once per submission attempt and reused for every retry of that attempt. Its first 6 characters appear in the email subject as '#xxxxxx' so Matt can spot a repeat. Optional in native posts (static pages cannot make one): the subject tag is then '#no-js'.

reference._rule: Generated by the function (UTC date + 4 random characters from the alphabet, crypto-random). Never accepted from a client except as the 'ref' of a file post, where it must match the signed file token.

attribution._rule: The page reads ONLY these query parameters (e.g. /website-brief/?from=planning-meeting, /contact/?area=wirral&interest=website), keeps a value only when it is in the allowlist, and sends {attribution:{...}} (JSON) or attr_from / attr_area / attr_interest hidden fields (native). The function drops anything else silently. Private metadata: it appears in the email only, never in the build pack. No other tracking.

_doc: { "field": "<key>", "in": ["<v1>", "<v2>"] }    single-choice answer is one of the values
{ "field": "<key>", "filled": true }               text non-empty after sanitising / list has a kept item / checkbox ticked
{ "sibling": "<itemKey>", "filled": true }         inside a repeatable group: another field of the SAME item is filled
{ "files": "any" }                                  at least one file is declared in the brief's files manifest

showWhen: the browser shows the field only while the condition is true and sends only the values of fields that are shown (it makes any removal of an answered follow-up explicit to the customer). The function NEVER drops a value because of showWhen: a follow-up that arrives while its condition is false is kept and flagged as a conflict in the email and missing-information.txt (lossless for the no-JavaScript form, which shows every field).
requiredWhen: the field is required only while the condition is true. The function evaluates it on the values exactly as received (nothing stripped).

Order rule: a showWhen condition may name only fields that come EARLIER in the same form's field list (no forward references, so no cycles). The browser evaluates showWhen in field order and treats a hidden field as empty (it will not be sent), so e.g. materialPermission follows proofDetails, which follows proofAvailable.

files.limitsNote: Up to 8 photos or files, each up to 3 MB: JPEG, PNG, WebP or HEIC photos, or PDF documents. Larger JPEG, PNG and WebP photos are made smaller on your device before sending.
files._sniffRule: Content decides the type, never File.type. Try the types in the order listed; a type matches when EVERY entry in its magic list matches ('hex' = lower-case hex bytes, 'ascii' = the bytes of that ASCII string, at that byte offset). For the heif family the 4 ASCII bytes at offset 8 (the ftyp major brand) must also be in majorBrands, and no compatible brand in the ftyp box (4-byte entries from offset 16 to the box size read big-endian at offset 0, capped at 64 bytes) may be in rejectCompatibleBrands. Read at least the first 64 bytes.
files._typeRule: The declared type must equal the sniffed type, except inside the same family (image/heic and image/heif are interchangeable). The file NAME's extension (case-insensitive) must be one of the extensions of ANY accepted type (so a renamed 'photo.png' that is really a JPEG is accepted as a JPEG); the attachment is always named with the sniffed type's canonicalExtension.

resize._rule: Only files over maxBytes are re-encoded, in the browser (canvas -> JPEG). Transparency is flattened onto white. Re-encoding drops embedded metadata such as location. If the result is still over maxBytes, try each fallback step in order; if still too large the file is refused with messages.files.tooLargeAfterResize. HEIC/HEIF and PDF are never re-encoded: over maxBytes they are refused with messages.files.tooLarge. Files at or under maxBytes are sent unchanged, including any embedded metadata (the build pack README tells Matt to strip metadata before publishing).
